image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Triceratops skull sculpture or fossil replica mounted on a stand in an outdoor setting with green foliage in the background. The image focuses heavily on the head, showcasing the three horns and the large bony frill. The body is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays two large brow horns and one smaller nasal horn, consistent with Triceratops morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostral bone forms a distinct beak shape typical of ceratopsians.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the skull; the body and limbs are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is prominently visible behind the skull, appearing solid and broad.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) with visible texture and marginal structures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No skin or body is visible to verify scale patterns or quills.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in this head-only shot.
The tail is not visible in the frame.

artifact_observations.location: Eye socket and interior of the mouth/beak area
artifact_observations.reasoning: The interior of the eye socket appears as a flat, uniform void without depth or anatomical detail, suggesting a simplified 3D model or sculpture rather than a biological entity. The beak interior also lacks complex texture.

The jaw structure seems to float slightly disconnected from the main skull mass near the hinge, and there is a visible metal support rod underneath, indicating this is a museum mount/sculpture, which creates a structural discontinuity compared to a living animal.
